value.title: Daemon CPU and memory: 240% CPU, 8-11 GB churn, unbounded tap files
value.summary: Found 2026-10-29: the machine daemon (main d459dda, 75 seats) runs at 200-280% CPU and swings between 8 and 11 GB RSS within a minute of a fresh start; pane-signal tap files total 3.2 GB (largest 380 MB) and are never trimmed.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Live on 2026-10-29. Daemon pid 29541 (12.5 h up): 239% CPU, RSS 7.8 GB, then 10.4 GB a minute later (+2.5 GB/min). After `just bounce-rs` (pid 95125): 8.8 GB RSS at +15 s, then 10.2 / 11.0 / 10.3 GB, at 212-280% CPU. So it is a high plateau with heavy churn, not a slow leak: something reads or allocates gigabytes per pass. pij-fleet#62 recorded the daemon at about 45% idle CPU, so this is a large regression or a scaling cliff. A 3 s `sample` shows time in `BgWorker::observe_completions` (reads and JSON-parses every one of the ~210 records in ~/.pij-rs/bg on each pass), `TmuxAdapter::drain_pane_tap` (opens every tap file on every observer tick), the tmux control client's reply reader, sqlite, and the daemon_log copier. `~/.pij-rs/pane-signals` holds 273 tap files totalling 3.2 GB: `cat >>` appends forever, and they are truncated only on a fresh attach. The machine has 128 GB, so this is not yet a freeze risk, but it costs cores, Defender scanning (every open()) and battery. Today's merges touched this path: #73 (control mode), #81, #83, #84. Rulings: assets/rulings.md.

sections.name: goals
value: Name, with profiles, what burns the daemon's CPU and memory.
Daemon idle CPU well under one core, and RSS bounded and flat with the current fleet.
Tap files are bounded on disk.

sections.name: non_goals
value: daemon.log rotation (#90), unless the same fix covers it.

value.claim: Diagnosis before fixing. Profile the live machine daemon read-only (macOS `sample`, `vmmap --summary`, `heap`/`footprint` if useful, `pij-rs --json ping`, per-thread CPU) and attribute its CPU and allocation to code paths with numbers, in assets/evidence/diagnosis.md. Say whether it is a regression from a specific merge today (#73 control mode, #81, #83, #84) or a scaling cliff (seats, tap sizes, bg records), with evidence: e.g. replay a captured workload against older builds in a private daemon on a private tmux server. Send the prime the diagnosis before fixing.
value.note: D1-D5 attributed with sample numbers; cliff, not a merge; replay table in lg-0002; D6 found by the replay (lg-0007).

value.claim: Fix the named hot paths. Each fix is launch-free and bounded: no per-tick full-directory reads where an index or notification will do, no per-tick open/read of every tap where only changed taps need it, no unbounded buffers. Every fix cites the diagnosis line it answers.
value.note: F1-F6, each citing its D line; launch-free; red/green lg-0003..lg-0007.

value.claim: Bounded tap files. A pane tap's file cannot grow without bound: rotate or truncate once the daemon has consumed it (keep correctness of offsets), with a stated per-pane cap. Existing oversized files are trimmed safely on startup. Test the offset math across a truncation.
value.note: TAP_TRIM_BYTES 1 MiB at first quiet drain; offsets across truncation tested on real tmux; orphan sweep with per-server ledger.

value.claim: Cost (AGENTS.md § Resource cost). Before/after on the live machine daemon: CPU% over 60 s, RSS at +15 s/+60 s/+10 min, `pij-rs --json ping` spawns, `just spawn-rate`, and `du -sh ~/.pij-rs/pane-signals`. Targets: idle CPU under 50% of one core with the current fleet, RSS flat (not climbing) and under 1 GB, or a stated, justified number. The prime takes the deployed reading.
value.note: Private-daemon after: CPU 62% -> 1.4%, RSS 5.6 GB climbing -> 15 MB flat; live before recorded. Deployed reading: prime, post-merge.

value.claim: Docs. docs/how describes the daemon's steady-state cost per seat (CPU, memory, file growth), how to measure it, and the tap-file bound.

Proof. Every behaviour change has a test RED on main (quoted) and green on the branch; where a test can't express it, a measured before/after on a private daemon with a recorded workload. Mutants on each fix. Scoped cargo tests, `just rust-check`, clippy -D warnings, fmt; GitHub CI green on the exact head. Anything not run is NOT RUN with its reason.

value.title: Find and fix the daemon's CPU and memory burn
value.brief: One phase: profile the live daemon read-only, name the hot paths with evidence, fix them with launch-free and bounded designs, cap tap-file growth, measure before/after, docs, mutants, PR. CS 4.
